SMTO-CMP-0028 — The AI's proof that the task worked only repeated its own words

GUID: e9b33323-71b6-4929-88f8-4899cb7c0918
Slug: completion-self-assertion-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI tried to prove the task was done with output that just repeats text it wrote, like a command that prints "Done". That doesn't show anything really changed, so SMTO asked for a real check.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to look at the actual result, such as reading the file or checking the service. A real check shows whether the change happened, which printed text cannot.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, look at the thing you asked to change yourself, or expand the task to see what each step returned. You can confirm whether the work really happened before asking for anything else.
  3. Send a message asking SMTO to check the current state and show you what it finds. Only ask for the change again if that check shows it's missing. This confirms the result without repeating a change that may already be in place.

What success looks like

  • The task finishes as Completed and the AI's reply points to a real check, such as file contents or a status it read.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask for the change to be made again until you've confirmed it isn't already there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because the cited receipts have evidence_type self_assertion (literal shell output, or stdout that only reflects authored or input text), which cannot establish an external observation.

What this means

  • A comparison relies on a self_assertion receipt, or all cited receipts only repeat authored/input-reflected statements. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A comparison relies on a self_assertion receipt, or all cited receipts only repeat authored/input-reflected statements.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect evidence_type and source provenance to distinguish an actual observation from echoed instructions.

How to fix it

  • Inspect evidence_type for the cited operation IDs in completion_feedback. Have the model obtain an independent observation (read the file, query the service, or run a command whose output is computed rather than echoed) and cite that receipt or a successful effect; literal echo output never qualifies.
  • Use observed external evidence rather than an operation’s unsupported self-assertion.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Authoritative observation supports the claim without treating repetition as proof.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
